responses.response: Push upstream only the reusable workspace assets: .github/skills/create-relationship/SKILL.md and projects/shared/spec-context.c4, and only after confirming they are generic and contain no local or private context. Keep projects/payments/system-model.c4 local because anything under projects/project is project-specific. Keep README.md local as well, because repository-level docs are not part of the normal shared upstream sync surface.

Safe sequence: commit the generic skill improvement locally if needed, fetch the upstream reference branch, create a sync branch from c4-template/main, bring over only the generic skill file, do a confidentiality and genericity review, commit only that file, then push the sync branch and open a PR to c4-template/main. Do not push directly from main.

Fetch c4-template main, then subtree pull into .github and projects/shared with squash, and push origin main afterward. Use squash to keep the imported upstream history compact and easier to review instead of pulling in a long chain of upstream commits.

Treat projects/shared/spec-containers.c4 as usually syncable, but not automatically syncable. Verify that another derived repository can use it without knowing local domain context, that it contains no project names, private architecture, secrets, or customer details, that it is a workspace-level improvement rather than a one-off workaround, and that you can explain it as a reusable fix. Then review the exact diff and ensure only that generic file is carried onto the sync branch.

Safest recovery: rebuild the sync branch from a clean upstream base and carry over only the generic file. Fetch upstream, create a clean replacement branch from c4-template/main, bring over only the good generic skill file from the contaminated branch, review for genericity and confidentiality, confirm the project-specific model file and README are absent, then commit and push the clean branch. If you must repair the existing branch instead, restore the local-only files to c4-template/main before committing the cleanup.
